English: to share, to divide and take
Example Sentence: 이 케이크를 세 명이서 나눠 가지자.
Sentence Translation: Let's divide and share this cake among the three of us.

Sentence Translation: The company is closed today because it is a holiday.

Etymology: 지 못하다 (cannot) + ? (question mark denoting rhetorical command)
Example Sentence: 당장 방을 치우지 못해?
Sentence Translation: Won't you clean your room right now?

English: it seems to be / I guess it is
Etymology: 이 (to be) + ㄴ가 (question ending) + 보다 (to guess/see)
Example Sentence: 저 사람이 새로 온 선생님인가 봐요.
Sentence Translation: I guess that person is the new teacher.

Etymology: 빙글 (mimicking a turning or spinning motion)
Example Sentence: 아이가 신나서 마당을 빙글빙글 돌고 있어요.
Sentence Translation: The child is excited and spinning round and round in the yard.

Example Sentence: 그는 책상 위에 가방을 툭 던졌다.
Sentence Translation: He tossed his bag lightly onto the desk.

Example Sentence: 그 슬픈 뉴스를 듣고 정말 마음이 아팠어요.
Sentence Translation: My heart hurt so much after hearing that sad news.

Etymology: 어찌하다 (to do somehow) + ㄹ 수 없다 (cannot) + 이 (adverb maker)
Example Sentence: 비가 너무 많이 와서 어쩔 수 없이 약속을 취소했다.
Sentence Translation: It rained so much that I had no choice but to cancel the plans.

English: to be startled, to jump in fright
Example Sentence: 뒤에서 갑자기 소리가 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
Sentence Translation: I was startled because a sound suddenly came from behind.

Etymology: 주렁주렁 (sound/look of many heavy things hanging)
Example Sentence: 포도나무에 포도가 주렁주렁 열렸어요.
Sentence Translation: Grapes are hanging in clusters on the grapevine.

Example Sentence: 우리는 난로가에 모여 오순도순 이야기를 나눴다.
Sentence Translation: We gathered by the stove and chatted harmoniously.

Example Sentence: 나쁜 짓을 하면 결국 벌을 받게 됩니다.
Sentence Translation: If you do bad things, you will eventually be punished.

English: sincerely / from the bottom of one's heart
Example Sentence: 여러분의 도움에 진심으로 감사드립니다.
Sentence Translation: I sincerely thank you all for your help.

Etymology: 돌다 (to turn/return) + 아 (connector) + 가시다 (to go - honorific)
Example Sentence: 할아버지께서 작년 겨울에 돌아가셨습니다.
Sentence Translation: My grandfather passed away last winter.

Etymology: 욕심 (greed) + 이 (subject marker) + 많다 (to be many/much)
Example Sentence: 그 아이는 장난감에 대한 욕심이 너무 많아요.
Sentence Translation: That child is too greedy when it comes to toys.

Example Sentence: 내일 여행을 가서 아이들이 무척 신이 났어요.
Sentence Translation: The children are very excited because we are going on a trip tomorrow.

Etymology: 찰싹 (sound of a flat object hitting)
Example Sentence: 파도가 바위에 찰싹 부딪히는 소리가 들렸다.
Sentence Translation: I heard the sound of the waves smacking against the rocks.

Etymology: 펑 (sound of an explosion or popping)

Sentence Translation: The balloon popped with a bang, so I was startled.
